newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA falls further after broker downgrade.
newsitem.headline: SIA falls further after broker downgrade.

text.p: Shares in Singapore Airlines Ltd fell further on Monday afternoon after the research arm of leading local brokerage DBS Securities cut its recommendation on the stock.

SIA's foreign shares, followed most closely by fund managers, stood at Singapore $13.00, down S$1.00, at 0840 GMT. At 0800 GMT, just before the downgrade was announced, the foreign shares stood at S$13.20.
DBS cut its recommendation on SIA's local shares to accumulate from buy, and its recommendation on the foreign shares to reduce from accumulate following poor interim results.

SIA earlier reported a bottom-of-consensus 7.2 percent rise in its net profit to S$560.5 million for the six months to September 30. Its operating profit fell 11.4 percent to S$467.6 million, reflecting a fall in yields.
DBS said in its daily briefing report to clients it expected SIA's full-year operating profit to be affected by lower yields and higher jet fuel costs.
"SIA's FYMar97 interims were disappointing and below market expectations," the report said.
